# AstryxDialog { #anylumino.AstryxDialog }

```python
AstryxDialog(children=None, *, open=True, inline=True, **props)
```

Render Astryx dialog content inline in notebook output.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name     | Type       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Default   |
|----------|------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| children | ChildInput | Dialog body content. Pass a widget, a sequence of widgets, or a mapping of slot names to widgets.                                                                                                                                                              | `None`    |
| open     | bool       | Initial open state synchronized through ``value``.                                                                                                                                                                                                             | `True`    |
| inline   | bool       | Whether dialog content renders inline instead of using native modal behavior.                                                                                                                                                                                  | `True`    |
| **props  | Any        | JSON-safe Dialog props. Useful keys: width, maxHeight, position, variant, purpose, className, and style. anylumino manages open state through value, inline mode, and child content. See Astryx component docs: <https://astryx.atmeta.com/components/Dialog>. | `{}`      |

## Notes {.doc-section .doc-section-notes}

The wrapper defaults to inline rendering to avoid modal focus-management
conflicts inside Jupyter output areas. Set ``inline=False`` only when the
surrounding notebook environment can safely host modal dialogs.
